newsitem.title: USA: U.S. help-wanted ad index rose to 84 in September.
newsitem.headline: U.S. help-wanted ad index rose to 84 in September.

text.p: The U.S. help-wanted advertising index rose to 84.0 in September against a reading of 81.0 in August, the Conference Board said on Thursday.

In the last three months, the volume of help-wanted advertising fell in six of the nine U.S. regions. The greatest decline was in the Mountain region, followed by the South Atlantic, East North Central and West North Central regions, the Conference Board said.

"The pace of job growth is likely to continue at relatively high levels into 1997, bolstering consumer confidence," Conference Board economist Ken Goldstein said in a statement. "Job growth, along with rising wage income, could translate into a pickup in consumer spending in the final months of 1996."

While the East North Central states are struggling to regain the strength they recorded earlier this year, strong labor market recoveries are underway in the Middle Atlantic and New England regions, the Conference Board said in its report.
